title: Geometric Phase Field Modeling for Adaptive Machine Learning
abstract: This paper explores the application of geometric phase field theory to enhance the robustness and generalization capabilities of machine learning models. Current machine learning paradigms often struggle with overfitting and sensitivity to initial conditions. We propose a novel framework that transforms the learning process into a geometric phase space, facilitating the identification of underlying patterns and improving model performance. This approach leverages the inherent mathematical properties of geometric phase fields to create a more adaptable and reliable system. The system aims to mitigate the limitations of traditional statistical methods by incorporating a geometric lens that actively explores the model space. We present a detailed theoretical analysis and preliminary implementation demonstrating the potential benefits of this framework.

title: 基于量子纠缠的超分辨率成像
abstract: This paper explores the potential of utilizing quantum entanglement for advanced imaging techniques, specifically focusing on the development of a novel high-resolution imaging system. We investigate how quantum entanglement, a phenomenon where two or more particles become inextricably linked, can be harnessed to facilitate instantaneous information transfer. This research proposes a method for rapidly transmitting details within an image, thereby surpassing the limitations of current image reconstruction technologies. The core concept revolves around exploiting quantum entanglement to establish a dynamic link between sensor data and the image reconstruction process, ultimately enabling the creation of images with unprecedented resolution. This work details the theoretical framework, proposed experimental setup, and preliminary results demonstrating the feasibility of this approach. We emphasize the potential of this technology to revolutionize imaging across various fields, including microscopy, medical imaging, and potentially even advanced materials analysis.

title: Based on Quantum Coherence: Adaptive Neural Networks
abstract: This paper introduces a novel neural network architecture termed the Adaptive Neural Network based on Quantum Coherence (ANQNQC). The core claim of this work is that real-time monitoring and dynamic adjustment of quantum coherence distribution within a neural network can lead to a more efficient and robust learning process compared to traditional deep learning models. The underlying mechanism involves integrating "quantum coherence sensors" into each neuron, enabling the measurement of its internal quantum state coherence. This sensor data is fed in real-time to a control module employing reinforcement learning algorithms, which dynamically adjusts neuron connection weights, activation thresholds, and quantum state modulation parameters to optimize coherence distribution. The network incorporates error correction coding, utilizing quantum coherence as an error signal for self-correction. This approach aims to reduce computational complexity, minimize information redundancy, and enhance resilience to noise and perturbations. The research represents a paradigm shift by leveraging quantum phenomena within neural networks, potentially overcoming the computational bottlenecks of classical networks and opening new avenues for efficient computation based on quantum mechanical principles. ---

title: Title: Temporal Feedback Loop for Neural Network Training
abstract: This paper investigates a novel temporal feedback loop for neural network training, addressing the limitations of static learning rates. We propose a mechanism that dynamically adjusts the learning rate based on the observed error distribution over time, fostering a more adaptive and robust training process. The core of this approach involves a continuous monitoring of the error landscape and a feedback mechanism that minimizes the error through a carefully orchestrated learning rate adjustment. The paper presents a detailed theoretical analysis and implementation of this algorithm, demonstrating its efficacy in improving convergence speed and stability compared to traditional methods. The benefits of this temporal feedback loop are explored, including enhanced generalization capabilities and reduced sensitivity to initial conditions.

title: Dynamic Topology Networks via Quantum Algorithms
abstract: This paper investigates the application of quantum algorithms to the construction of dynamic topology networks. We propose a novel approach to network design that leverages the inherent properties of quantum topology to enhance computational efficiency. The core mechanism revolves around utilizing quantum algorithms to dynamically generate and manipulate network topology, offering a significant advantage over traditional static network building methods. This research explores the potential of this approach in distributed computation, focusing on the benefits of adaptability and optimized network structure.

title: Neuro-Symbolic Reasoning with Continuous Knowledge Representation
abstract: This paper investigates the challenges of integrating continuous and discrete knowledge within neuro-symbolic reasoning systems. We propose a novel architecture that leverages continuous knowledge representation, specifically through the use of autoencoders, to create smooth transitions between neural and symbolic domains. The core mechanism involves encoding prior knowledge into continuous embeddings and then constructing a neuro-symbolic framework to utilize these embeddings during reasoning. Our approach aims to address the limitations of existing systems that often struggle to effectively utilize continuous data alongside symbolic logic. We demonstrate the potential for improved reasoning performance by enabling a more nuanced and flexible representation of knowledge, allowing the system to handle uncertainty and ambiguity more effectively. The paper outlines the architecture, the knowledge encoding process, and the reasoning process, highlighting the key components and their interactions.

title: Quantum-Driven Topological Data Analysis (Q-TDA)
abstract: Quantum-Driven Topological Data Analysis (Q-TDA) represents a paradigm shift in data analysis, leveraging the unique properties of quantum mechanics to uncover hidden patterns and correlations within complex data sets. This paper proposes a novel quantum algorithm designed to effectively explore and interpret topological data, offering a fundamentally different approach compared to traditional methods. We delve into the core mechanism of utilizing quantum superposition and entanglement to achieve a deeper understanding of the underlying topological structure of the data, aiming to unveil patterns that are obscured by classical analysis. This research explores the potential of Q-TDA to revolutionize data discovery and analysis across various domains, including but not limited to medical imaging, materials science, and network security. The paper outlines the core concepts, proposed algorithm, and initial results demonstrating the potential of this approach.

title: Ethical and Legal Principles in PE Technology
abstract: This chapter examines the ethical and legal implications of using recording and assessment technologies in Physical Education (PE), showing how the datafication of movement and performance reshapes pedagogical relationships and requires new forms of governance. Drawing on the data lifecycle, core ethical principles, and international regulatory frameworks, it argues that monitoring is only legitimate when grounded in transparency, data minimization, proportionality, and proactive accountability. The chapter also provides operational guidance, risk-management procedures, and checklists to support responsible implementation in both educational and research contexts.

title: Trust-aware hybrid QKD–PQC key management for quantum-safe communication networks
abstract: The security of today’s communication networks rests on public-key primitives—RSA and elliptic-curve Diffie–Hellman—that a large quantum computer would break with Shor’s algorithm, while the “harvest-now, decrypt-later” threat means traffic captured today is already at risk. Two defences exist but each is incomplete: quantum key distribution (QKD) offers information-theoretic security yet fails open under eavesdropping or channel loss, while post-quantum cryptography (PQC) is computationally secure and always available but lacks physical-layer guarantees. This paper presents a dual-layer, trust-aware key-management framework that uses BB84 QKD as the primary channel and a Ring-LWE/Kyber key-encapsulation mechanism as a quantum-safe fallback, governed by a controller monitoring the quantum bit-error rate (QBER) and a trust signal. When intercept-resend eavesdropping pushes the QBER past the 11% abort threshold—reached at roughly 40% interception—the controller falls back to PQC, holding secure availability at 100% where a QKD-only system degrades to 78.5%. The lattice fallback is cheap ( ≈ 0.47 m per operation) and Kyber-768 gives 192-bit quantum-safe security. Coupling the fallback and re-keying rate to a node trust score integrates physical-layer and computational security into one always-available, forward-secure key-management layer. To our knowledge, this is the first key-management framework in which a single network-layer trust signal jointly governs QKD/PQC layer selection and the re-keying cadence, unifying physical-layer eavesdropping detection, computational quantum-safety, and forward secrecy in one cross-layer policy.

title: Clean Accuracy Does Not Guarantee Provenance Robustness: A Prospective Codec-Stress Evaluation of Audio Attribution
abstract: Audio provenance attribution - which system produced a synthetic utterance - is reported at near-ceiling accuracy on clean benchmarks, yet audio reaching an analyst has usually been transcoded. We report a prospectively registered measurement of closed-set attribution after single-stage codec transport, with the analysis region fixed from fidelity metadata before any attribution model was trained. On two corpora, in-support losses reach 53.5 [43.5, 63.6] and 70.3 [63.0, 77.5] Macro-F1 points for WavLM-Base+, and 61.0 [56.8, 65.1] and 49.8 [41.6, 57.9] for W2V2-BERT 2.0, under simultaneous component-level bands. Degradation is strongly condition- and representation-dependent: within one in-support grid WavLM losses run from -0.4 to +53.5 points, and the two encoders differ beyond a prespecified +/-5-point margin at six of twelve conditions. A clean-qualified ECAPA-TDNN and a Proxy-Anchor head degrade comparably, so the effect is not confined to one representation family or a weak linear head. The registered matched-fidelity comparison was not estimable on this grid, and waveform and perceptual measures order the conditions differently: MP3 at 8 kbit/s ranks mid-grid on SI-SDR but last on PESQ-WB while causing the largest loss. For the tested tasks, corpora, representations and codec grid, a clean accuracy figure does not by itself characterise deployment robustness.

title: ReactVAU: A Slow-Fast Decoupled Framework for Streaming Video Anomaly Understanding
abstract: In this paper, we propose ReactVAU, a Slow-Fast Decoupled Framework for real-time streaming Video Anomaly Understanding (VAU). Existing VAU methods rely on offline inference with global temporal sampling, which violates causality and prevents deployment in live surveillance streams. Conversely, general streaming video models satisfy causal access but dilute rare transient anomalies during memory compression and often invoke heavyweight MLLMs uniformly over long normal intervals. React VAU addresses this gap with three synergistic components: a lightweight Fast Detection Module based on Spatial Grid Folding (SGF) for continuous anomaly filtering; an Anomaly-Aware Persistent Memory (AAPM) that protects critical visual cues from temporal decay; and a heavyweight Slow Reasoning Module that remains dormant during normal streams and is awakened only by suspicious events for semantic verification and causal description. Extensive experiments on multiple benchmarks demonstrate that ReactVAU operates under strict streaming constraints while simultaneously achieving competitive performance in both anomaly detection and causal reasoning, alongside significantly enhanced computational efficiency by minimizing heavyweight MLLM invocations. Project page is available at https://huiyuiui.github.io/React_VAU/

title: BioBERT-Derived Clinical Text Representations and Sparse Principal Components of Multi-Omics Data for Breast Cancer Survival Prediction: A Leakage-Controlled Cross-Validated Benchmark
abstract: Abstract Background Reported performance for multi-modal cancer prognostic models is frequently obtained from a single train–test partition and without comparison against a simple clinical baseline. We evaluated an integrated framework combining language-model representations of structured clinical records with high-dimensional multi-omics data under a leakage-controlled protocol. Methods Clinical variables from 589 TCGA-BRCA patients were converted to natural language sentences and encoded with BioBERT; DNA methylation, RNA, miRNA and protein data were reduced by Sparse principal component analysis. Clinical-only, multi-omics-only and integrated feature sets were evaluated with Cox proportional hazards, XGBoost and random survival forest (RSF) using five repetitions of stratified five-fold cross-validation with pooled out-of-fold predictions. Models were compared against a marginal Kaplan–Meier null and a conventional age-and-stage Cox model, with differences assessed by paired bootstrap. Results Among 589 patients with 88 deaths (14.9%; median follow-up 33.7 months), the integrated RSF model performed best (Harrell’s C 0.685, 95% CI 0.620–0.754; Uno’s C 0.748), exceeding the conventional clinical Cox model (0.637, 0.559–0.707). The ordering integrated > clinical-only > multi-omics-only held in all nine feature-set by algorithm comparisons and at all three component settings tested. The integrated model significantly outperformed every multi-omics-only model ( P = 0.008–0.044) but not clinical-only models (ΔC = 0.037, P = 0.128). Brier scores approached a null reference at 2 and 3 years and improved modestly at 5 years. Conclusion Integration produced the highest discrimination and exceeded a conventional clinical model, but the gain over clinical features within the same pipeline was not statistically resolvable at this event count. Reporting simple baselines, null-model calibration and cross-validated estimates should be standard in multi-modal prognostic modelling.

title: Semantic Drift in Iterated LLM Paraphrase Chains: Model Architecture, Scale, Quantization, Serving Infrastructure, and Prompt Engineering
abstract: When large language models (LLMs) operate in sequential pipelines, each agent paraphrasing the output of the previous one, the cumulative signal diverges from the original in ways that are poorly understood. We study this semantic drift with a telephone-game protocol: a single text is paraphrased 30 times by the same model and cosine similarity to the original is measured at every step. Two complementary datasets are analysed. A cross-family sweep covers 17 models from 8B to 123B parameters with ablations of KV-cache precision (fp16 vs.\ q8\_0 on 10 Qwen3 variants), temperature, and 20 system prompts. A within-family sweep holds the architecture fixed and covers the Qwen3.5 family at 7 sizes (0.8B-122B) and 3 GGUF precision levels, four 4-bit formats of the same 35B mixture-of-experts checkpoint (GGUF, AWQ, NVFP4, GPTQ-Int4) on three serving stacks, five temperatures, and the same 20 system prompts on six configurations plus an out-of-family control. Together the datasets comprise 2,627 completed 30-step chains and roughly 79,000 scored inferences. We find: (1) a stability hierarchy across families - three occupied tiers on a four-band scale, with no model in the Degraded band - with a 0.67 gap in final similarity between the best and worst models and catastrophic tipping-point failures in the weakest; (2) within one family, a capacity threshold near 4B parameters below which no configuration is reliable, and above which the ordering by size is irregular; (3) a discrete runaway-thinking failure mode in which a model with reasoning enabled spends its entire 16,384-token budget inside the thinking block and returns nothing - absent wherever reasoning was disabled but affecting 15-54% of chains on the two stacks that ran Qwen3.5 with its default reasoning on, concentrated in 4-bit builds, small models, the short stimulus, and constraining system prompts; (4) 4-bit quantization formats of identical weights that differ by up to 0.26 on the short stimulus among the chains that survive runaway (two to five per arm, with format and serving stack covarying), while precision level is non-monotonic throughout; (5) KV-cache precision and temperature effects that are directionally mixed and small for stable models, while below the threshold low temperature raises the runaway rate to 100% of chains; and (6) system-prompt effects that range from invisible (spread <0.01 on the most stable cross-family model) to dominant (spreads of 0.3-0.7 within the Qwen3.5 family), with prompt rankings that transfer between some configurations (rho up to 0.83) and not others (rho\approx0 against the control model). Fixing the sampling seed does not reproduce a chain on any of these stacks, so all statistics are reported over independent samples with bootstrap intervals. title: 基于概率的群论优化算法
abstract: This paper introduces a novel probabilistic group optimization algorithm designed for optimizing machine learning models, particularly within high-dimensional datasets. The core idea is to represent parameter adjustments as probability distributions, enabling a more robust and adaptable optimization process. We propose a method incorporating probabilistic weighting, allowing the algorithm to effectively handle noisy data and improve model generalization. The algorithm leverages probability distributions to guide the optimization process, offering a significant improvement over traditional optimization techniques. The paper details the algorithm's design, its advantages, and provides a comparative analysis with existing methods, highlighting its potential for enhancing machine learning model performance. The core mechanism centers on the introduction of probabilistic weighting, which facilitates the exploration of parameter space with greater flexibility and robustness.

title: Quantum Reservoir Computing for Dynamic System Identification
abstract: This paper explores the application of quantum reservoir computing (QRC) to dynamic system identification. Traditional reservoir computing utilizes randomly connected recurrent neural networks to process time-series data, offering a computationally efficient approach to modeling complex, nonlinear dynamics. However, the inherent limitations of classical reservoir computing, particularly regarding the extraction of nuanced features, are addressed by integrating quantum mechanical principles. Specifically, we investigate the utilization of a quantum reservoir – a system of interacting qubits – to perform non-linear feature extraction. The core mechanism leverages quantum superposition and entanglement to represent complex dynamics more efficiently than classical counterparts. The aim is to demonstrate that QRC possesses the potential to surpass classical methods in both speed and accuracy for dynamic system modeling. This work lays the groundwork for future research into exploiting quantum computing for enhanced time-series analysis and control applications.

title: On Interpretable Reinforcement Learning for Ecosystem Modeling and Control
abstract: This paper explores the application of interpretable reinforcement learning (IRL) to the modeling and control of ecological systems. Traditional reinforcement learning models often suffer from a lack of transparency, making it difficult to understand and trust their decision-making processes. This research proposes a novel approach that integrates IRL with reinforcement learning, enabling the construction of more reliable and understandable ecosystem models and the development of finer-grained control strategies. The core of this approach utilizes rule-based, interpretable agents to simulate ecosystem behavior and employs reinforcement learning algorithms to optimize control policies, while simultaneously providing explanations for the underlying decision-making process. We demonstrate the potential of this method through a conceptual framework and highlight the advantages of incorporating interpretability into complex systems modeling and control. The ultimate goal is to move beyond "black box" models and towards more robust and trustworthy ecological management solutions.

abstract: This paper introduces a novel reinforcement learning (RL) algorithm based on dynamic adaptive learning strategies. Traditional RL methods often rely on predefined reward functions, limiting the algorithm's ability to efficiently discover optimal policies. Our proposed algorithm dynamically adjusts the learning strategy based on environmental feedback and model error, enabling more effective decision-making and control. We present a mechanism that allows the agent to continuously refine its policy through this adaptation, overcoming the limitations of static reward functions. This approach offers improved robustness and adaptability in complex environments.

abstract: This paper presents a novel dynamic information entropy gradient algorithm leveraging the inherent quantum properties of entangled states. Traditional information entropy gradient methods often rely on static parameter adjustments, limiting their efficiency and adaptability. We propose a method that dynamically adjusts the gradient based on the quantum state, allowing for a more efficient and versatile optimization process. The core mechanism involves utilizing quantum entanglement to provide a mechanism for continuous and adaptive gradient estimation, ultimately improving the performance of the algorithm across a range of datasets. The research explores the potential of this approach to overcome the limitations of static gradient methods and offers a promising pathway for enhancing the optimization capabilities of machine learning models.

title: Non-Linear Matrix Space Theory: Dynamic Adaptive Algorithm
abstract: This paper introduces a novel theory and algorithm for rapidly learning and optimizing complex nonlinear systems, particularly when dealing with large datasets. The core concept revolves around a dynamic matrix space, leveraging adaptive algorithms to dynamically adjust the space's parameters. We propose a framework that combines matrix space manipulation with self-adaptive optimization techniques, aiming to significantly improve learning efficiency and optimization outcomes in diverse applications. This work addresses a critical challenge in machine learning: the need for robust and adaptable solutions to highly complex systems. The proposed method offers a fundamentally different approach, shifting the focus from static representations to dynamic space manipulation, potentially leading to improved performance in scenarios where traditional methods struggle. This research explores the potential of this approach through detailed mathematical modeling and practical demonstration, emphasizing its effectiveness in real-world scenarios.

title: 高阶线性结构体的自适应优化算法
abstract: This paper presents a novel self-adaptive optimization algorithm based on a high-order linear structure, specifically leveraging the properties of high-order linear matrices and linear chains. The algorithm aims to enhance optimization efficiency and convergence speed, particularly in scenarios involving large datasets and high-dimensional spaces. We introduce a dynamic adjustment mechanism to guide the optimization process by leveraging the characteristics of the linear structure. The core concept revolves around strategically positioning and manipulating these structures to effectively navigate complex optimization challenges. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through theoretical analysis and empirical validation on a range of benchmark problems. This paper establishes a new paradigm for optimization, offering a compelling solution for tackling computationally intensive problems across diverse domains.

title: Relational Embedding Learning with Graph Memory Networks
abstract: This paper proposes Graph Memory Networks (GMNs) as a novel approach to relational embedding learning. Traditional embedding methods often struggle to capture complex relationships between entities, particularly within heterogeneous data. GMNs address this limitation by incorporating a graph memory component, enabling the explicit representation and reasoning about relationships. The core idea is to extend the architecture of memory networks with a graph structure, allowing for the simultaneous processing of data points and relational information encoded within the graph. We demonstrate that this combination leads to significantly improved relational embeddings compared to standard memory networks and other existing embedding techniques. The presented framework offers a flexible and powerful tool for learning embeddings in scenarios where relational understanding is paramount, such as knowledge graph completion, social network analysis, and recommendation systems. The primary contribution lies in the integration of graph structures into memory networks to facilitate relational reasoning and improved embedding quality.

title: A Neuromorphic Computing-Based Accelerator for Quantum Algorithm Acceleration
abstract: This paper explores the design and potential of a neuromorphic computing-based accelerator for quantum algorithms. The core idea is to leverage the inherent parallelism of neuromorphic hardware to significantly speed up the computationally intensive aspects of quantum algorithms. We propose a methodology for decomposing complex quantum algorithms into a set of parallelizable tasks, which are then mapped onto a neuromorphic architecture. The architecture utilizes the key characteristics of neuromorphic systems—namely, synaptic plasticity and dynamic connection adjustment—to optimize the execution of these quantum tasks. This approach aims to address the significant computational bottleneck currently limiting the practical application of many quantum algorithms. The design incorporates key mathematical concepts from quantum mechanics and neuromorphic computing, providing a framework for future research and development in this emerging field. The paper outlines the architectural considerations, the mapping strategies, and discusses the potential for achieving substantial performance gains. ---

title: 基于自适应的量子纠缠计算算法
abstract: Quantum entanglement is a fundamental phenomenon in quantum mechanics, exhibiting correlations between particles that cannot be explained by classical physics. It holds immense potential for quantum technologies, including quantum computing and quantum communication. However, the practical implementation of quantum algorithms often faces significant challenges due to the fragility of quantum states and the difficulty in maintaining entanglement. This paper introduces a novel quantum entanglement computation algorithm, leveraging adaptive strategies to optimize computation efficiency and accuracy. We propose a dynamic adjustment of the quantum state's measurement strategy based on the entangled state's complexity and desired precision. The core mechanism involves learning and adapting the quantum state's transformation based on the entanglement's inherent characteristics. This adaptive approach significantly enhances the algorithm's ability to effectively utilize quantum resources and achieve superior performance compared to static approaches. The paper details the algorithm's implementation, performance analysis, and potential impact on quantum computation.

title: Quantum-Inspired Stochastic Search for Complex Optimization
abstract: This paper introduces a novel stochastic search algorithm, termed Quantum-Inspired Stochastic Search (QISS), which leverages principles derived from quantum mechanics to address the challenges of complex optimization problems. Traditional stochastic search algorithms often struggle with high dimensionality and non-convex landscapes, leading to inefficient exploration and premature convergence. QISS overcomes these limitations by incorporating a "quantum-inspired" operator that mimics the probabilistic nature of quantum measurement. This operator allows the algorithm to simultaneously explore multiple potential solutions based on weighted probabilities, effectively simulating a quantum state. The core of QISS lies in its ability to dynamically adjust these probabilities, fostering a more comprehensive and efficient search process. The algorithm's design directly addresses the inherent uncertainties associated with complex optimization, offering a fundamentally different approach compared to conventional stochastic methods. We demonstrate the algorithm's potential through theoretical analysis and outline its key components and operational principles. The results suggest that QISS can significantly enhance the efficiency of stochastic search algorithms, particularly for high-dimensional, non-convex optimization problems.

title: Adaptive Parallel Algorithm Scheduler Based on Quantum Degradation Analysis
abstract: This paper presents a novel adaptive parallel algorithm scheduler designed to optimize the execution of quantum algorithms on imperfect quantum hardware. The core idea leverages quantum degradation analysis to dynamically adjust the scheduling of tasks and resource allocation. Traditional parallel algorithm schedulers often operate under the assumption of ideal quantum hardware, failing to account for the inherent noise and errors present in real-world quantum devices. Our approach utilizes real-time monitoring of quantum hardware degradation, specifically focusing on metrics like single-qubit fidelity, to guide the scheduling process. The scheduler employs a feedback loop, continuously assessing hardware performance and adapting the algorithm execution order and resource assignment accordingly. This adaptive strategy aims to mitigate the impact of quantum noise and maximize the overall fidelity of the final computation. The theoretical framework is presented, and the underlying mathematical concepts are detailed. The effectiveness of the proposed scheduler is illustrated through a conceptual model, showcasing its ability to improve performance in the presence of varying levels of quantum degradation. The primary contribution lies in the integration of quantum degradation analysis directly into the scheduling process, leading to a more robust and efficient execution of parallel quantum algorithms.

title: Quantum-Inspired Neural Networks with Entanglement-Based Feature Interactions
abstract: This paper investigates the potential of quantum-inspired neural networks (QINNs) leveraging the principles of quantum entanglement to enhance feature interactions within artificial neural networks. Traditional neural networks often struggle with complex, non-linear relationships between features, leading to suboptimal performance. We propose a novel architecture where nodes are initially randomly entangled, and training dynamically adjusts the entanglement structure based on the input data. This approach mimics the correlated behavior observed in quantum systems, allowing for more efficient and nuanced feature representation. The core idea is to replace the static connections of conventional neural networks with dynamically evolving entanglement relationships. We explore the mathematical framework underlying this approach, focusing on the probabilistic nature of entanglement and its impact on information flow. The model is designed to learn complex patterns by exploiting the inherent correlations introduced by entanglement. Experimental results (simulated) demonstrate the potential of QINNs to outperform conventional neural networks in tasks requiring intricate feature interactions, suggesting a promising direction for future neural network design.

title: Adaptive Neuron Networks: Dynamic Neuron Type Generation
abstract: This paper investigates a novel approach to enhancing the expressiveness and learning capabilities of artificial neural networks through dynamic neuron type generation. The core idea is to analyze the activity patterns within a neural network and, based on this analysis, automatically generate new neuron types. This process is driven by a machine learning-based adaptive algorithm that adjusts neuron parameters and introduces new neuron types, effectively creating a dynamic and evolving neural network architecture. Unlike traditional approaches that rely on manually designed neuron types, this method allows the network to adapt and optimize itself based on its operational experience. The research demonstrates the potential of this technique to improve network performance in complex tasks, offering a more flexible and robust solution compared to static network designs. The primary contribution lies in treating neuron type generation as a continuous, dynamic process, ultimately boosting the network's adaptability and learning proficiency.

title: Quantum Entanglement-Based Distributed Storage and Computation Protocol
abstract: This paper presents a novel protocol for distributed storage and computation leveraging the principles of quantum entanglement. The core claim is to design a protocol capable of securely storing vast amounts of data and efficiently performing computations by exploiting the inherent properties of entanglement. The central mechanism involves constructing a distributed network based on entangled qubits. This approach offers potential advantages over classical distributed systems in terms of security and computational capabilities. The protocol is described in detail, outlining the key steps involved in data storage, retrieval, and computation. The protocol utilizes a multi-party entanglement scheme and incorporates error correction techniques to enhance reliability. This work lays a foundational framework for future research in quantum distributed systems and highlights the possibilities of quantum computing for large-scale data management. The proposed protocol aims to demonstrate the feasibility of utilizing quantum entanglement for secure and efficient distributed processing. ---

title: TDDN: Text-aligned Diffused DINO Network for Puzzle Understanding
abstract: Structured visual reasoning, such as image puzzles, demands fine-grained visual perception, an ability current Vision Language Models (VLMs) lack. VLMs built on CLIP-based ViT backbones trade fine-grained detail for high-level semantics, and we show this loss propagates downstream. To recover it, we fuse DINOv3 and CleanDIFT representations into a perception encoder (DiffusedDINO) and align it with RoBERTa-L, yielding a text-aligned model TDDN that preserves this perceptual advantage: with frozen backbones and only sim590K alignment pairs, TDDN matches CLIP on image-text retrieval, surpassing it on three of four settings. It does so while more than tripling CLIP's dense-prediction accuracy (ADE20K 5.20 to 18.11 mIoU, COCO-Stuff 7.35 to 24.44), despite CLIP's massive training corpus. TDDN leads on segmentation benchmarks among general-purpose contrastive encoders, including SigLIP,2. We further introduce Puzzle Perception, a segmentation and visual question answering dataset that probes fine-grained spatial understanding, on which TDDN doubles CLIP's segmentation accuracy (11.04 to 22.51 mIoU).

title: Decentralized Safe Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning via Predictive Shielding
abstract: Environments are increasingly populated by multiple robots performing independent tasks with limited prior knowledge of each other. Deploying such multi-agent systems presents significant challenges. Specifically, shifts in deployment states compared to training data can lead to poor policy performance and compromised safety. While safety shields exist to mitigate these risks, they are typically reactive, which degrades performance near unseen obstacles,and centralized, limiting their scalability. To address this, we propose a decentralized framework that integrates predictive shielding with model-based finite horizon Q-learning. This approach allows agents to safely adapt their pre-trained policies during deployment. Furthermore, to mitigate livelocks in symmetric scenarios, we introduce a communication- free protocol for conflict resolution

title: Phase-and-First-Arrival VLM Feedback for Sparse-Reward Reinforcement Learning in Surgical Manipulation
abstract: Sparse outcome feedback limits what robots can learn from unsuccessful attempts at complex manipulation. Failed multi-stage surgical attempts can contain grasps, lifts, or transfers worth reusing. In sparse-reward reinforcement learning, terminal rewards collapse such attempts to the same outcome, while scalar vision-language model (VLM) ratings reveal neither what progress merits credit nor when it occurred. We introduce phase-and-first-arrival feedback: one VLM query per recorded episode identifies the furthest visually verified task phase and when that phase is first reached, allowing the learner to reuse partial behavior and localize credit. We instantiate it in SurgPhaseBench, a phase-structured suite spanning rigid and deformable tasks, and evaluate it in simulation and hardware. Across five simulated tasks, our method reaches 75.2% mean success, compared with 52.1% for a reward based on Contrastive Language-Image Pre-training (CLIP) using the same visual input; the advantage persists when only the feedback representation changes. On hardware, the same record supports autonomous block picking and slip recovery. Together, these results show that trajectory-level visual supervision can preserve partial progress while providing the temporal credit needed for sparse-reward control.

title: Stochastic neural networks for quantum devices
abstract: Abstract This work presents a formulation to express and optimize stochastic neural networks as quantum circuits in gate-based quantum computing. Motivated by a classical perceptron, stochastic artificial neurons are introduced and combined into a quantum neural network. The Kiefer-Wolfowitz algorithm in combination with simulated annealing is used for training the network weights. Several topologies and models are presented, including shallow fully connected networks, Hopfield Networks, Restricted Boltzmann Machines, Autoencoders and convolutional neural networks. We also demonstrate the combination of our optimized neural networks as an oracle for the Grover algorithm to realize a quantum generative AI model.

title: Natural Language Processing for Discussion Platforms
abstract: Online participation platforms and digital discussion spaces have become central arenas for public discourse, particularly in times of crisis such as the COVID-19 pandemic. While these environments expand opportunities for civic engagement, they are frequently characterized by incivility, misinformation, and unstructured exchanges. Drawing on the concept of deliberation, defined by the core dimensions of rationality, civility, interactivity and equality, this thesis investigates how Natural Language Processing (NLP) methods can be leveraged to foster more respectful, reasoned, and inclusive online discussions. The dissertation addresses five central aspects: (i) the current approaches in applying NLP to online discussion platforms, (ii) the optimization of smaller language models for efficient real-time deployment, (iii) the integration of NLP-based interventions into discussion platforms, (iv) user perceptions of Artificial Intelligence (AI)-supported moderation and assistance, and (v) the measurable effects of such interventions on discussion quality. First, a systematic review provides a comprehensive overview of existing NLP applications in political and civic online discussions, identifying established approaches and tasks that could potentially be used to support discussions (see Chapter 4). Second, the thesis develops and evaluates methods to improve the efficiency and effectiveness of small Transformer-based models, particularly Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers (BERT), for tasks relevant to online deliberation. This includes adapting pre-training strategies for argument similarity detection (ArgueBERT, see Chapter 5) and optimizing fine-tuning procedures for classification performance (MaxPoolBERT, see Chapter 6). In addition, the Additive deliberative Quality score with Adapters (AQuA) is introduced to assess the deliberative quality of user contributions (see Chapter 7). This model, along with a comment recommendation module based on stance detection, has been integrated into an online discussion platform and tested in a large-scale, real-time experiment (see Chapter 8). The findings provide insights into the technical integration of AI-supported tools into online discussion platforms, as well as into users’ perceptions of such systems and their observed effects in a specific participatory context. By combining perspectives from computer science, political science, and communication science, this interdisciplinary work contributes to the development of AI-supported tools that aim to support deliberative processes in digital public spheres.

title: Approximate Equilibrium Play in 4-Max Shove-or-Fold Poker: A Delayed-Linear Weighted-Averaging MCCFR Study at 8BB Effective Stacks
abstract: This technical note presents validated shove and call ranges for 4-player all-in-or-fold poker at 8 big-blind effective stacks. The strategy was produced using delayed-linear weighted-averaging Monte Carlo Counterfactual Regret Minimization (MCCFR), trained from iteration zero to 4,000,000 across two independent seeds and merged through the FullHouse production adapter. The resulting Production v2 policy passed a four-stage adoption protocol incorporating structural validation, NashConv evaluation, whole-game comparison against the previous production policy, and a frozen stress-cell regression. The latter returned a mixed result and is retained as adverse evidence. The published ranges should therefore be interpreted as a validated finite-compute estimate of equilibrium play rather than a formal proof of Nash equilibrium. Mixed-strategy frequencies displayed in the PDF are rounded to the nearest 25% for readability; the underlying policy retains exact frequencies. Feedback, corrections, methodological criticism and edge-case reports are welcome.

title: Quantum Entanglement for Gene Sequence Prediction
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a peculiar phenomenon in quantum mechanics, offers a potentially revolutionary approach to gene sequence prediction. This research investigates the utilization of entanglement to enhance the accuracy of genetic sequence prediction, specifically addressing the limitations of traditional computational methods. We propose a novel method that leverages the unique properties of entangled quantum states to minimize error during the probability calculation of gene sequences. This paper explores the potential of this approach, emphasizing its advantages in handling large datasets and significantly improving prediction accuracy. The core mechanism centers around introducing entanglement to mitigate the inherent computational challenges of genetic sequence analysis.

title: 基于量子态的自适应神经元网络架构
abstract: This paper introduces a novel neural network architecture, termed "Quantum-Aware Network" (QAN), that leverages the unique properties of quantum states to enhance learning and reasoning capabilities. The QAN architecture utilizes quantum entanglement and superposition to facilitate efficient parameter learning and improve the network's overall performance. We explore the potential advantages of this approach, particularly in scenarios demanding complex data analysis and rapid adaptation. The paper details the design of a quantum state network and discusses the theoretical foundation underpinning its potential benefits. Further, we present experimental results demonstrating the QAN's enhanced learning and inference capabilities compared to conventional neural networks, validating the core claims of improved parameter learning and enhanced network capacity.

title: Title: Topology-Driven Quantum State Partitioning – Beyond Quantum State Decomposition
abstract: Topology-Driven Quantum State Partitioning presents a novel approach to quantum state partitioning that leverages topological invariants as a guiding principle. The core mechanism centers on constructing a system where states exhibiting similar topological properties are naturally separated, offering a potential pathway to identifying inherently stable quantum states. This research addresses limitations in existing approaches by explicitly incorporating topological structure into the partitioning process, leading to a fundamentally different methodology with the potential to unlock new insights into quantum information theory and quantum algorithms. The method's emphasis on the structure of quantum states differentiates it from traditional decomposition techniques and promises to provide a more robust and insightful framework for quantum state analysis.

title: 自适应量子纠缠的拓扑结构建模
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a cornerstone of quantum information processing, exhibits a remarkable degree of fragility. Traditional approaches often struggle to fully exploit the inherent properties of entangled states, leading to limitations in computation and error correction. This paper introduces a novel framework for modeling quantum entanglement based on dynamic topological structures, aiming to enhance the stability and controllability of entangled states. We propose a mechanism that dynamically adjusts the topology of the entangled state, leveraging this structure to suppress quantum noise and improve overall information processing. The core claim is that incorporating this dynamic topology allows for more precise control and manipulation of quantum information through a measurable "topological structure." This research explores the potential of this approach to overcome limitations inherent in existing quantum computing models and opens up avenues for more efficient and robust quantum information handling.

title: Quantum Error Correction for Distributed Sensor Networks
abstract: This paper explores the application of quantum error correction (QEC) techniques to construct highly resilient distributed sensor networks. Traditional sensor networks suffer from significant data corruption due to noise and environmental factors, limiting their precision and reliability. Leveraging the principles of QEC, this research proposes a framework for encoding sensor data using quantum error-correcting codes and transmitting this encoded data across a distributed network. The subsequent decoding process, employing appropriate error correction algorithms, recovers the original, uncorrupted data. The core claim of this work is that the integration of QEC with distributed sensor networks enables the attainment of unparalleled accuracy and robustness in environmental data acquisition and transmission. We outline the key components of this system, focusing on the selection of suitable QEC codes and the design of efficient decoding strategies. The potential impact of this approach on various applications, including environmental monitoring, structural health monitoring, and precision agriculture, is discussed. ---

title: Non-Linear Adaptive Optimization (NLOAO)
abstract: This paper introduces Non-Linear Adaptive Optimization (NLOAO), a novel optimization algorithm designed to dynamically adjust optimization parameters based on input data. Traditional optimization methods often rely on fixed parameters, limiting their adaptability to varying data distributions. NLOAO achieves this adaptability through an iterative optimization process, systematically refining parameters to find optimal configurations. The paper details the core mechanism, including a self-adaptive parameter adjustment strategy, and explores its potential benefits in enhancing optimization efficiency and performance. The study demonstrates the effectiveness of NLOAO through a series of simulations and analysis, highlighting its ability to handle complex data patterns and achieve superior results compared to traditional methods.

title: 基于自适应的图神经网络的复杂系统模拟
abstract: This paper introduces a novel framework for complex system simulation based on adaptive graph neural networks (GNNs). Traditional GNNs are often static and struggle to effectively model dynamic systems. We propose a dynamic GNN framework that adapts to system parameters and simulation goals, dynamically adjusting network parameters and structure to enhance simulation accuracy and efficiency. This approach addresses the limitations of static GNNs by enabling real-time optimization. The core mechanism leverages self-adaptation to refine the network's representation, leading to improved simulation results across a range of scenarios. We present a methodology for parameter tuning and structural optimization using a combination of gradient descent and reinforcement learning techniques, demonstrating its effectiveness through simulations of a simplified dynamic system. The results demonstrate significant improvements in accuracy and efficiency compared to baseline methods.

title: Dynamic State Generation and Optimization
abstract: Quantum state generation and optimization is a crucial area of research in quantum computing, aiming to automate the process of creating and refining quantum states. This paper introduces a novel algorithm, QuantumStateDynamicOptimization (QSDO), which leverages the inherent dynamics of quantum systems to generate and optimize states efficiently. The core mechanism of QSDO involves iteratively adjusting quantum states based on predefined optimization criteria, minimizing the required manual intervention. This algorithm significantly reduces the number of adjustments needed to achieve desired outcomes, offering a promising step towards more practical and scalable quantum technologies. This paper details the algorithm's architecture, optimization techniques, and preliminary experimental results demonstrating its effectiveness.

title: Predictive Modeling with Multi-Scale Nonlinear Models
abstract: This paper presents a novel predictive modeling approach leveraging multi-scale nonlinear models. Traditional machine learning techniques often struggle with capturing the complexity of intricate systems, leading to "catastrophic forgetting." Our model addresses this challenge by decomposing the system into distinct scales, employing separate models for each scale, and integrating their predictions to enhance overall accuracy. We demonstrate that this approach significantly outperforms traditional methods across a range of simulated and experimental datasets, indicating a substantial improvement in prediction fidelity. This research explores the potential of integrating multi-scale information to overcome limitations of single-scale models, ultimately offering a more robust and accurate solution for complex system prediction.

title: Quantum Machine Learning with Entanglement Resource Optimization
abstract: This paper investigates the potential of optimizing entanglement resources within quantum machine learning (QML) algorithms. Traditional approaches often treat entanglement as a readily available, cost-free resource. However, this research posits that strategic management and optimization of entanglement are crucial for significantly enhancing the performance and accuracy of QML models. The core concept involves building a quantum machine learning model, analyzing the algorithm's entanglement requirements, and then employing optimization techniques – specifically, quantum annealing-inspired algorithms – to determine the optimal allocation of entanglement. This approach aims to improve computational efficiency and overall accuracy by leveraging entanglement more effectively. We demonstrate, through theoretical analysis and algorithmic design, that a deliberate focus on entanglement resource optimization can represent a transformative step in advancing the field of quantum machine learning. The results suggest that entanglement, when properly managed, is not merely a byproduct of quantum computation but a key strategic element for achieving superior QML performance.

title: Self-Correcting Digital Circuit Design via Evolutionary Algorithms
abstract: Digital circuit design faces significant challenges regarding reliability due to inherent design complexities, manufacturing variations, and environmental factors. Traditional design methodologies often rely on extensive manual verification and debugging, which are time-consuming and error-prone. This paper proposes a novel approach to digital circuit design leveraging evolutionary algorithms for automated self-correction. The core idea is to embed a verification process directly within the design optimization loop, creating a self-correcting system. An evolutionary algorithm iteratively modifies both the circuit topology and the parameters of individual gates. Performance metrics and simulated error injection are used to guide the algorithm toward a robust and reliable design. The system's ability to adapt and correct errors during the design process offers a significant advantage over conventional methods, potentially leading to higher yields and reduced development costs. The key innovation lies in the integrated design and verification paradigm, enabling the creation of circuits that are inherently more resistant to errors. Mathematical formulations and algorithmic steps are detailed to illustrate the system's functionality.

title: TempFinRAG: Multimodal Temporal Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Point-in-Time Financial Question Answering
abstract: Financial question answering is often treated as document question answering, although financial evidence is both multimodal and time-dependent. Semantically equivalent facts expressed in narrative text, tables, page images, or Extensible Business Reporting Language (XBRL) should support consistent answers, whereas a disclosure may support a query only after becoming public. We formalise this combination as crossmodal evidence symmetry under a causal temporal boundary and introduce TempFinRAG, a multimodal temporal retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) framework for point-in-time financial question answering. Given a question, company, and as-of date, the framework enforces the information boundary defined by U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) filing availability; aligns page layout, text, table structure, and XBRL facts; retrieves time-valid evidence; executes auditable financial calculations; and generates a cited answer. A verifier checks temporal validity, claim support, numerical consistency, and the need to abstain. We further introduce TempFinQA, a point-in-time evaluation protocol built from public filings and XBRL facts, and evaluate the framework on complementary evidence-grounded, numerical, conversational, and multi-table benchmarks. On TempFinQA, TempFinRAG improves answer accuracy from 66.7% to 78.9% over hybrid RAG while reducing temporal evidence leakage from 10.8% to 1.7% and hallucination from 17.3% to 7.9%. Reliable financial question answering therefore requires consistent treatment across evidence representations and deliberately asymmetric access across time.

evidence.title: TempFinRAG: Multimodal Temporal Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Point-in-Time Financial Question Answering
evidence.abstract: Financial question answering is often treated as document question answering, although financial evidence is both multimodal and time-dependent. Semantically equivalent facts expressed in narrative text, tables, page images, or Extensible Business Reporting Language (XBRL) should support consistent answers, whereas a disclosure may support a query only after becoming public. We formalise this combination as crossmodal evidence symmetry under a causal temporal boundary and introduce TempFinRAG, a multimodal temporal retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) framework for point-in-time financial question answering. Given a question, company, and as-of date, the framework enforces the information boundary defined by U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) filing availability; aligns page layout, text, table structure, and XBRL facts; retrieves time-valid evidence; executes auditable financial calculations; and generates a cited answer. A verifier checks temporal validity, claim support, numerical consistency, and the need to abstain. We further introduce TempFinQA, a point-in-time evaluation protocol built from public filings and XBRL facts, and evaluate the framework on complementary evidence-grounded, numerical, conversational, and multi-table benchmarks. On TempFinQA, TempFinRAG improves answer accuracy from 66.7% to 78.9% over hybrid RAG while reducing temporal evidence leakage from 10.8% to 1.7% and hallucination from 17.3% to 7.9%. Reliable financial question answering therefore requires consistent treatment across evidence representations and deliberately asymmetric access across time.

title: Evidence-Calibrated Preference Alignment for Geoscience and Climate Instruction Following
abstract: Geology licensing exams, graduate climate textbooks, web-scale climate claims, and ocean-coast reports all require language models to mix magnitudes, SI units, spatial scale, and calibrated uncertainty. Domain continued pre-training plus supervised fine-tuning raises multiple-choice accuracy, yet a uniform preference loss still rewards fluent slogans over literature-grounded, physically consistent answers. We present ECGA, evidence-calibrated geoscience alignment. Evidence-grounded claim routing (EGCR) splits a response into verifiable claims, retrieves geoscience and climate passages, and reweights the preference pair by support-versus-refute scores. A unit-scale consistency regularizer (USCR) down-weights winners that break unit conversion, spatial extent, or time-horizon constraints. Uncertainty-calibrated preference aggregation (UCPA) maintains factual, uncertainty, and actionability heads and gates them by question type. Built on the K2 geoscience recipe and a TRL preference loop, ECGA improves GeoBench NPEE accuracy from 39.9 to 43.4, ClimaQA-Gold MCQ from 75.92 to 79.18, Climate-FEVER accuracy from 52.17 to 54.85 versus SimPO, and Pirá 2.0 MCQ from 86.6 to 89.2, with the largest gains on hypothetical climate items and SUPPORTS recall.

title: Impact Propagation and Inconsistency Resolution in a Large Ontology
abstract: Large ontologies constantly evolve to adapt to their original purpose. Ontology evolution refers to the process of modification in response to a change in the domain or its conceptualization. This evolution must address changes in the ontology and guarantee the consistency of both the ontology and all dependent objects. Therefore, the impacts of a change in an ontological entity must be managed before beginning any evolution process. Maintaining large ontologies, such as the NCI Thesaurus and the Gene Ontology, is complex because it is often entrusted to groups of experts who only support the part of the ontology they created. Another problem related to ontology evolution is tracking the propagation of inconsistencies among the entities of the modified ontology. Existing work does not adequately address this important aspect. We propose an approach that partitions a large ontology to track propagation impacts and resolve inconsistencies. Our approach first determines communities in the ontology, marks impacted entities and uses a Markov decision process to resolve inconsistencies.

title: Gen Z Empowerment, and Resistance to AI-Driven Recommendations
abstract: The quick adoption of AI in digital marketing has changed the way customers get exposed and react to customized recommendations. Although AI-based systems increase convenience and level of prediction, increasing concerns about privacy, manipulation, and algorithmic visibility have affected consumer behavior, especially among the generation Z. The research paper explores the factors that affect the resistance to AI-driven recommendations by considering the influence of AI awareness and transparency perception and evaluates the issue of ethical concerns and how trust in AI systems moderates this aspect. The research is based on the Stimulus Organism Response (S-O-R) framework (Mehrabian and Russell, 1974) that conceptualizes the awareness of AI and ethical issues as technological stimuli that drive psychological appraisals that result in resistance behaviors. The structured questionnaire was used to collect data on 70 Gen Z respondents who use AI-based recommendation platforms actively. To test direct and moderating effects, multiple regression was used to test them. The results indicate that the ethical issues make the opposition to AI-generated recommendations much higher and the confidence in AI systems greatly decreases the resistance behaviors. The correlation of AI awareness with resistance is marginal positive, which means that awareness does not inevitably prompt resistance but can perhaps increase it. The effect of ethical concerns is also partially cushioned by the moderating role of trust. By setting the focus on consumer adoption aside and defining the role of ethical governance and trust-building mechanisms in the setting of AI mediation, the study contributes to the literature on AI marketing by emphasizing the significance of resistance to AI marketing.

title: Generalized quantum neural modules for high-dimensional local quantum feature learning
abstract: Abstract Quantum convolution offers a natural inductive bias for extracting local structure from high-dimensional data, yet its practical reach is constrained by direct feature-wise encoding, which ties broader receptive fields to wider quantum registers. This raises a central question: can local quantum representations retain their predictive content when receptive-field growth is redirected from circuit width to sequential processing on a compact register? Generalized quantum neural modules address this question through incremental data upload, partitioning each receptive field into ordered batches, preserving a single evolving quantum state across successive encode–entangle stages, and reusing shared trainable transformations as the local window moves across the input. State-vector experiments on controlled three- and four-dimensional motif tensors, MNIST images, and selected UCF101 action videos show that moderate serialization substantially narrows the active register while preserving the predictive behaviour of direct encoding; more aggressive partitioning, by contrast, reveals a progressive trade-off between sequential depth and within-batch feature interaction, with mixed CRZ–CRX entanglement providing the most effective fixed-width configuration. Together, these results delineate a practical operating regime for high-dimensional local quantum learning and show that receptive-field scaling can be managed through a coordinated choice of upload granularity, entangling structure, information retention, and execution depth.

title: FrogNano: Training a 4B Coding Agent via Online Task Synthesis
abstract: We present FrogNano, a 4B coding agent designed to tackle software engineering (SWE) tasks efficiently and effectively, even under resource-constrained environments. It is post-trained exclusively via RL on around 1,500 SWE environments with synthetic tasks. A key ingredient for improving performance is an online task synthesis pipeline that creates tasks calibrated to the frontier of learnability for the current checkpoint. This report provides evidence that competitive small coding agents can be trained with synthetic tasks alone, without traditional distillation from larger models, and that generating tasks at the learnability frontier of the current agent is important. We report details on the training methodology, evaluations across diverse environments, and in-depth analyses, serving as a foundation for our ongoing exploration of lightweight yet capable coding agents that can run on minimal hardware.

title: Efficient Exploration Is Enough
abstract: This work introduces an alternative view of efficient exploration and studies its theoretical and empirical implications in the absence of extrinsic rewards. Specifically, we define efficient explorers as agents that prioritize generating generalizable experience, i.e., data that supports learning models capable of predicting and adapting across the environment. This allows us to analyze efficient exploration through the lens of prediction and generalization. Theoretically, we demonstrate that optimally efficient explorers naturally schedule their trajectories to visit the most informative and learnable regions first. Empirically, we show that optimizing for these agents gives rise to an automatic curriculum of progressively more complex behaviors, even in relatively simple environments. These results indicate that pursuing this purely intrinsic objective alone is enough to drive the emergence of highly sophisticated behaviors. We believe that this new framework provides a principled mechanism by which agent-environment systems may sustain an open-ended process of increasingly complex behavior without external rewards, tasks, or objectives.

title: Performance Evaluation of Post-Quantum Cryptography in Satellite Security Architecture
abstract: Satellite systems rely on a robust yet light weight cryptographic solution for the security of ground systems, communications links, Telemetry, Tracking and Command (TT&C), payloads, onboard systems and associated subsystems. Cryptography ensures data integrity and overall security especially for satellites whose missions and data transmitted are in general and by global practices included in Critical National Infrastructures (CNIs). But emerging cybersecurity threats might render cryptographic solutions such as Rivest-Shamir-Adleman (RSA), Diffie–Hellman (DH) and Elliptic-Curve Cryptography (ECC) ineffective in securing space assets. Quantum cryptography offers a better solution to the emerging threats of relentless and sophisticated systems and adversaries. This paper evaluates the performance of Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC) when deployed. The research explored the various standards mapped out by the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) for PQC deployment. Current security architecture of satellite systems was compared to what the PQC solution will offer to these highly classified assets. The paper further explored algorithms in place and how effective they could be in the space industry. In the space sector, deploying PQC requires a beta analysis of its performance; which was explored in the third chapter of this work. Challenges and Deployment Considerations and Computational and Resource Constraints of PQC deployment was evaluated in the fifth and sixth sections of this work. The paper concluded by acknowledging the potential complexities in the eventual wholistic adoption and deployment of Quantum Cryptography.

title: Privacy-Enhanced Key-Value Data Collection for Large-Scale IoT Environments
abstract: Privacy-preserving data collection is essential for IoT environments, where massive volumes of key-value data are continuously generated and transmitted across distributed devices. Local Differential Privacy (LDP) provides protection without requiring trusted data collectors, but conventional mechanisms often introduce substantial estimation errors and reduced data utility, particularly for composite key-value structures. This work addresses these limitations through an accuracy-oriented privacy-preserving collection framework using a key-value dataset containing categorical keys and associated values collected over a defined observation period. The data is preprocessed by removing missing and duplicate records, validating key-value pairs, encoding categorical attributes, and applying normalization where required. The implemented models include Randomized Response, Generalized Randomized Response, Optimized Unary Encoding, and proposed hybrid mechanisms combining key and value perturbation with sampling-based processing. Performance is evaluated using privacy level, hit rate, estimation variance, precision, and utility preservation. Among the evaluated approaches, the proposed hybrid key-value perturbation mechanism achieves the highest hit rate and the lowest estimation variance, demonstrating improved estimation reliability under privacy constraints. The results indicate that coordinated sampling and perturbation can provide stronger privacy protection while maintaining high data utility, offering an effective approach for accurate and privacy-preserving keyvalue data collection in IoT environments.

title: Resource-Honest Quantum Computing for Fusion: Variational Landau-Damping Emulation and ADAPT-VQE Low-Activation Alloy Chemistry Against the Classical Frontier
abstract: Quantum computing is routinely invoked for fusion without a disciplined account of what is reachable now and what is a fault-tolerant-horizon problem. We supply that account for a specific machine — the Kronos Hyperion compact spherical-tokamak breeder (design point I_p=9.66 MA, Q=3.076, P_fus=85.04 MW, negative triangularity δ=-0.30, B_0=8 T, elongation κ=2.0, major radius R_0=1.20 m, aspect ratio A=2.5, centrepost peak field 16.84 T) and its distinct tandem-mirror burner — through two grounded demonstrations, a resource frontier, and a pre-registered honest negative. First, a genuinely kinetic collisionless phenomenon, Landau damping, is reproduced on a 5-qubit circuit: casting the linearized Vlasov–Poisson system in an asymmetrically-weighted Fourier–Hermite basis and folding in the Poisson closure yields a Hermitian generator whose unitary evolution is a legitimate Hamiltonian-simulation target, and the circuit reproduces the analytic Landau rate to 1–7% across three wavenumbers, landing the complex dispersion at /=1.4157-0.1534 i against the textbook 1.4156-0.1533 i. Second, an adaptive variational quantum eigensolver (ADAPT-VQE) reaches chemical accuracy (better than 1.6 mHa) on the transition-metal fragments of the candidate low-activation refractory alloys, four orders of magnitude below the ~300mHa spread of density-functional exchange–correlation choices, with a fixed-ansatz depth 4–14× shallower than unitary coupled cluster. A third strand is a genuinely measured quantum capability: an in-winding nitrogen-vacancy (NV) diamond magnetometer resolves a ~100 superconducting-quench step at a per-shot signal-to-noise ratio of ~1.5×10^9 (sensitivity 0.189/Hz, bandwidth 125), giving single-shot quench-precursor detection — but its headline femto/pico-tesla sensitivity is forfeited in the reactor vessel, a second pre-registered negative we keep rather than hide. The honest boundaries are explicit: under a representative noise model the field-energy observable decoheres to the maximally-mixed floor 1/32 and the damping signature is lost, so present-day noisy hardware shows no advantage; and while the linear collisionless kinetic operator is an early-fault-tolerant target (11–19 logical qubits, 10^5–10^6 non-Clifford gates), the nonlinear five-dimensional gyrokinetic problem that actually sets confinement remains a fault-tolerant-horizon target (~10^2 logical qubits, 10^9–10^13 non-Clifford gates), and the Harrow–Hassidim–Lloyd equilibrium linear solve — the single most-invoked ``quantum inner kernel'' — costs ~1.8×10^17 T-gates once read-in and read-out are counted, a boundary and not a route this decade. Against the classical frontier — nonlinear CGYRO gyrokinetics and a quantum-inspired matrix-product-state solver that runs 21.2× faster at bond dimension 7, is the only feasible method past bond dimension 10, and drives its error to 2.2×10^-10 at bond dimension 16 — the classical tool is cheaper at every scale demonstrated here. The contribution is a set of validated encodings, a rigorous numerical formulation, and an honest, dated resource map, not a claim of quantum advantage. Key results (frozen anchors): k = 0.30 0.50. Methods & codes: CGYRO, QAOA, VQE, ADAPT-VQE. Live verification: 8 gate validator(s) with live-recompute cards (5 reproduced, 3 estimated). See the Verification section and data/verification.csv. title: Quantum-Inspired Algorithms for Reinforcement Learning Policy Optimization
abstract: This paper investigates the potential of quantum-inspired algorithms to improve reinforcement learning (RL) policy optimization. Traditional RL methods often struggle with slow convergence and exploration challenges, particularly in complex environments. We propose a novel approach that draws inspiration from quantum mechanics, specifically superposition and entanglement, to address these limitations. Our algorithms aim to exploit superposition to simultaneously evaluate multiple action possibilities and utilize entanglement to model correlations between states, thereby accelerating the learning process. We present a framework for incorporating these concepts into RL, focusing on algorithmic design rather than a direct quantum simulation. The theoretical analysis suggests that our approach could significantly enhance exploration efficiency and, consequently, policy convergence rates. This work represents a direct application of quantum-inspired ideas to RL policy optimization, offering a potentially transformative pathway for developing more efficient and robust RL agents.

title: Neuro-Symbolic Reasoning for Robotic Navigation in Unstructured Environments
abstract: This paper explores the integration of neural networks and symbolic reasoning techniques to address the challenges of robotic navigation in unstructured environments. Current robotic navigation systems often struggle with the inherent complexity and unpredictability of real-world scenarios, particularly those lacking well-defined maps. We propose a neuro-symbolic framework that leverages the perceptual capabilities of neural networks – specifically, deep convolutional neural networks (DCNNs) – alongside the logical deduction and planning abilities of symbolic reasoning. The core idea is to use the DCNN to extract relevant features from sensor data (e.g., camera images) and then utilize these features as input to a symbolic planner, enabling the robot to generate a sequence of actions based on a predefined goal. This approach aims to overcome the limitations of purely data-driven methods (neural networks) and purely rule-based methods (classical planning) by combining their respective strengths. We outline the architecture of the system, focusing on the interaction between the perception and reasoning modules. The key contribution of this work lies in the development of a robust and adaptable navigation strategy that can handle uncertainty and dynamically adjust to changing environmental conditions. The paper concludes with a discussion of potential future research directions, including the incorporation of temporal reasoning and hierarchical planning.

evidence.abstract: This paper explores the integration of neural networks and symbolic reasoning techniques to address the challenges of robotic navigation in unstructured environments. Current robotic navigation systems often struggle with the inherent complexity and unpredictability of real-world scenarios, particularly those lacking well-defined maps. We propose a neuro-symbolic framework that leverages the perceptual capabilities of neural networks – specifically, deep convolutional neural networks (DCNNs) – alongside the logical deduction and planning abilities of symbolic reasoning. The core idea is to use the DCNN to extract relevant features from sensor data (e.g., camera images) and then utilize these features as input to a symbolic planner, enabling the robot to generate a sequence of actions based on a predefined goal. This approach aims to overcome the limitations of purely data-driven methods (neural networks) and purely rule-based methods (classical planning) by combining their respective strengths. We outline the architecture of the system, focusing on the interaction between the perception and reasoning modules. The key contribution of this work lies in the development of a robust and adaptable navigation strategy that can handle uncertainty and dynamically adjust to changing environmental conditions. The paper concludes with a discussion of potential future research directions, including the incorporation of temporal reasoning and hierarchical planning.

title: High-Dimensional Data Clustering Adaptive Clustering Algorithm
abstract: This paper introduces a novel adaptive clustering algorithm designed for high-dimensional data. Traditional clustering algorithms often struggle with the challenges posed by high dimensionality, requiring extensive parameter tuning. Our proposed approach dynamically adjusts the clustering parameters during the clustering process, allowing the algorithm to adapt to the unique characteristics of the data and achieve higher precision. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this algorithm through a series of experiments evaluating its performance on benchmark datasets. The core mechanism leverages a self-adaptative approach to optimize the clustering process, mitigating the issues associated with static parameter settings.
